PRIVACY & COOKIES

Website privacy and analytics

Last updated: 30 October 2026.

Who manages this website?

CurveMole is an open-source project maintained by Sebastiano Romi. For privacy questions or data-protection requests, contact romi@lens.unifi.it.

What information is collected?

The site is hosted on GitHub Pages. GitHub may process technical information needed to deliver pages, independently of CurveMole's optional analytics. See GitHub's privacy statement.

With your explicit permission, we use Google Analytics 4 (measurement ID G-WZS7HDJ5QB) to measure visits, pages viewed and aggregate usage trends. Depending on your device and settings, Analytics can process an online identifier, approximate location, browser/device information, and information about visits and interactions. We use it to improve the website, not to serve personalized advertisements.

Cookies and consent

Google Analytics is disabled by default and its scripts are not loaded before you select “Allow analytics.” If enabled, it may set first-party cookies such as _ga and _ga_* to distinguish browsers and sessions. Their default lifetime is up to two years, subject to browser policies. Analytics may involve processing by Google Ireland Limited and Google LLC, including international data transfers. See Google's privacy policy.

Your consent preference is saved in this browser's local storage under curvemole-analytics-consent-v1 for up to 180 days. This entry is used only to remember your choice. Rejecting analytics leaves the site fully usable. You may reopen the choice panel at any time from the home page; withdrawing consent stops future measurement and removes accessible first-party Analytics cookies from this site.

Manage analytics preferences ↗

Data retention and your rights

Analytics reporting and retention depend on the settings of the Google Analytics property; raw event-level data uses a limited retention period, whereas aggregate reports may remain available longer. You can ask for information about the retention settings and request access, erasure or other applicable GDPR rights using the contact address above. You may also submit a complaint to your supervisory data-protection authority.

Further information about Google's processing and settings is available in Google's Analytics data safeguards.
